item.text: {"rubric":[{"claim_id":"claim_1","claim_type":"core","weight":20,"statement":"`ParallelExecutor` snapshots the parent thread-local DSPy overrides and passes that override snapshot into every submitted worker.","span_ids":["s1"]},{"claim_id":"claim_2","claim_type":"core","weight":30,"statement":"When a worker receives overrides containing `usage_tracker`, the executor deep-copies that tracker before installing the overrides, so workers do not share the parent's tracker object.","span_ids":["s2"]},{"claim_id":"claim_3","claim_type":"core","weight":15,"statement":"`UsageTracker.get_total_tokens()` aggregates only the calling tracker's own `usage_data`, so a worker that returns `dspy.settings.usage_tracker.get_total_tokens()` reports usage from its locally installed tracker instance.","span_ids":["s2","s3"]},{"claim_id":"claim_4","claim_type":"supporting","weight":15,"statement":"The parallel usage-tracker test defines two tasks that add different token counts and confirms the returned prompt/completion totals differ by worker (`50/10` versus `80/15`).","span_ids":["s4","s5"]},{"claim_id":"claim_5","claim_type":"core","weight":20,"statement":"The parallel usage-tracker test expects the original `parent_tracker` to remain empty after the batch, showing DSPy does not merge worker tracker state back into the parent tracker.","span_ids":["s6"]}],"evidence":[{"span_id":"s1","path":"dspy/utils/parallelizer.py","start_line":159,"end_line":168},{"span_id":"s2","path":"dspy/utils/parallelizer.py","start_line":122,"end_line":130},{"span_id":"s3","path":"dspy/utils/usage_tracker.py","start_line":57,"end_line":65},{"span_id":"s4","path":"tests/utils/test_usage_tracker.py","start_line":355,"end_line":377},{"span_id":"s5","path":"tests/utils/test_usage_tracker.py","start_line":379,"end_line":391},{"span_id":"s6","path":"tests/utils/test_usage_tracker.py","start_line":393,"end_line":394}]}
